A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HALD study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations and proofs, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HALD evaluations on Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K, supervision ablations and semantic-consistency analyses, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds CIFAR-100/ImageWoof evaluations, an LPQLD comparison, feature visualizations and adaptive-scheduling results.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix D adds an optional adaptive scheduler: validation-accuracy stabilization triggers Soft-to-Hard switching, and an entropy plateau triggers Hard-to-Soft switching. The principal three-stage method, losses, label smoothing and CutMix remain unchanged. Describing its existing targets as heavily flattened hard labels is clarification, not another algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v3 Table 6 adds actual evaluations on CIFAR-100 and ImageWoof, extending coverage to additional general and fine-grained recognition settings. Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-1K and the original real-image subset experiments are retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds LPQLD as an evaluated comparator at IPC=10 and IPC=20. The existing SRe2L, RDED, FADRM, LPLD, GIFT, Soft-Only and Joint Objective comparisons remain; publication-year updates do not represent new baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluations include UMAP representations with silhouette scores and an adaptive-versus-fixed scheduling comparison using validation accuracy and entropy to control training transitions. The retained experiments preserve their documented preprocessing, 300-epoch budget, optimizer and hyperparameter tables. The PDFs do not establish that those original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds feature-separation analysis in Figure 4 and tests whether adaptive scheduling can approximate fixed scheduling in Appendix D/Table 19. Existing phase-order, phase-duration, smoothing and generation-method ablations remain. Teacher-consistency analysis moves from v1 Appendix C.1 into the main text; it is not newly added evidence.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly describes mean plus/minus standard deviation over three runs and states that random seeds are fixed. v3 removes these disclosures while retaining the plus/minus entries in Tables 1–2. This reduces statistical-reporting detail without establishing any actual change in run counts or seed handling.

E6.justification: v3 adds dataset, LPQLD, adaptive-scheduling and feature-separation results while retaining the main benchmark scores. Table 11 revises FADRM's smoothing results: accuracy at alpha=0.9 changes from 36.3 to 35.3, shifting its best tested rate from 0.9 to 0.8. v1 Table 6's JS-divergence values disappear from v3 Table 13; retained cosine values are merely rounded. Appendix storage tables also relabel MiB as MB without numerical conversion.

T1.justification: v1 Definition 1 defines LVSD through nonzero crop-prediction covariance. v3 Definition 3.1 substantially revises the central concept to finite-sample class-inversion risk, adding an oracle-error/variance decomposition and a Cantelli probability bound under a positive class margin. The principal loss, excess-risk and gradient-consistency proofs in Appendix B are otherwise substantially retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about sparse soft-label drift, corrective hard-label supervision and HALD's storage-efficient generalization. The headline 42.7% accuracy with 285M storage and 9.0-point advantage over LPLD is unchanged. The newly explicit approximately 100-fold storage reduction quantifies the previously reported storage figures.

C2.justification: The smoothing explanation changes from matching high-temperature teacher targets to accommodating ambiguous synthetic-image semantics. v3 also acknowledges dataset-specific tuning of fixed schedules, interprets the new feature clusters as evidence of reduced drift, and introduces method-specific risks involving hard-label noise, bias and over-calibration in its Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's reproducibility statement describing structured .yml configurations and planned preparation/training/evaluation scripts. Table 9 also loses its explicit IPC=10, SLC=100 and FADRM setting. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size and phase-duration details remain, as does the code link; an actual change in resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to LPQLD and UMAP and positions HALD against LPQLD experimentally. It removes the explicit discussion of EDC combining hard and soft objectives, although the EDC paper remains cited elsewhere. Numerous other reference changes are publication or bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory passages are condensed, contributions are enumerated, and ablation and analysis sections are reordered. Cross-architecture and real-data discussions are consolidated under Analysis, and teacher consistency moves into the main text. The appendix contents page and separate reproducibility/LLM-use statements disappear, but the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a predominantly single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout, substantially redistributing figures and tables. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 4 and three comparison tables are added, and the teacher-consistency table moves from the appendix. The calibration table also loses its JS-divergence columns.

improvement.justification: The added benchmarks, comparator and adaptive-scheduling test broaden the evidence and address practical tuning concerns. However, v3 removes run/seed disclosures and diagnostic values while leaving new experimental settings incompletely specified. Definition 3.1 also treats nonzero variance as sufficient for LVSD while defining absence through zero class-inversion probability, conditions that need not agree. These empirical gains and reporting/theoretical regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
